title: Getting started with Easel
seo: Getting started with Easel, the focus timer that reveals a painting
desc: Your first focus session in Easel, step by step: choose how long to focus, begin, and watch a painting from The Met emerge from the fog until it’s fully revealed at 0:00.
card: Your first focus session in Easel, step by step: choose how long to focus, begin, and watch a painting from The Met emerge from the fog until it’s fully revealed at 0:00.
lede: Easel is a focus timer with a reward you can see. Choose how long you’ll work, and a painting from The Met slowly emerges from the fog while you focus. Here’s your first session, from opening the app to the finished painting.
body:
The home screen

Everything starts on one quiet screen. From top to bottom:

  • Gallery (top left): the paintings you’ve uncovered.
  • Settings (top right): appearance, sounds, reminders, widgets’ daily goal and more.
  • What will you focus on? An optional line for what you’re working on.
  • Single or Pomodoro: one session, or four focus blocks with short breaks.
  • Focus for: 5, 15, 25, 45 or 60 minutes, or Custom for anything from 5 to 120.
  • Focus with: which paintings to draw from. All paintings surprises you.
  • Begin.

Your first session

  1. Choose a length. 25 minutes is a good start. Tap Custom to pick any length from 5 to 120 minutes on a wheel.
  2. Say what it’s for (optional). Type it in the line at the top, or leave it empty and Easel will ask you “What will you focus on?” when you tap Begin. See the focus question.
  3. Tap Begin. Easel picks a painting and loads it completely before the session starts, so the reveal never waits on your connection.
  4. Work. The painting clears from the centre outward as the minutes pass. The timer sits quietly at the top; you don’t need to watch it.
  5. At 0:00 the painting is fully revealed. A cream museum placard rises at the bottom with how long you focused, what for, the title, artist and date. Tap Done and it hangs in your gallery.

Where to go next

  • Focus sessions and the fog reveal: locking your phone, ending early, sounds.
  • Pomodoro: four blocks with breaks, a new painting each time.
  • Your gallery: every painting you’ve earned, with its museum label.
Lost in the app?

Every screen in Easel has a way back: the ‹ back button at the top left, the ⌄ chevron on Statistics, or a swipe down on sheets. You always return to the home screen. More in Troubleshooting.

title: Focus sessions and the fog reveal
seo: How Easel’s focus sessions and fog reveal work
desc: How a focus session works in Easel: the fog reveal, the timer, leaving the app or locking your phone, ending early, ambient music, sound effects and haptics.
card: How a focus session works in Easel: the fog reveal, the timer, leaving the app or locking your phone, ending early, ambient music, sound effects and haptics.
lede: A session is the heart of Easel: one painting, slowly revealed while you work. This guide explains what happens during a session and what you can do while it runs.
body:
How the reveal works

Each session hangs a painting behind a soft, drifting fog. As time passes, it clears from the centre outward. The pace is gentle at first and opens up towards the end, so the last minutes feel like an arrival. At 0:00 the painting is completely clear, corners included.

Above the painting you’ll see the remaining time and, if you set one, your intention. Both are faint on purpose: Easel wants you looking at your work, not the clock.

Leaving the app or locking your phone

Go ahead. The timer is anchored to the moment your session will end, not to ticks while the app is open, so it keeps true time while Easel is in the background or your phone is locked. Come back and the painting is exactly as far along as it should be.

  • While Easel is open on a session, it keeps the screen from dimming so you can watch the reveal.
  • On the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, a Live Activity shows the countdown. See Widgets and Live Activities.
  • If the session finishes while you’re away, the painting is waiting for you when you return.

Ending a session early

Tap End at the top right, then confirm. The painting won’t finish, so it isn’t added to your gallery, and the session doesn’t count towards your statistics or streak. In Pomodoro, ending early ends the whole set.

Sound, music and haptics

  • The speaker button (top left during a session) mutes or unmutes sound for the session.
  • Ambient music: quiet piano while a painting reveals. Turn it on in Settings → During a session.
  • Sound effects: the chime when a painting completes.
  • Haptic feedback: gentle taps on buttons and at the start and end of a session.

When the painting is revealed

At 0:00 the whole painting is clear, and a museum placard rises at the bottom of the screen: the session’s length and your intention, then the painting’s title, artist and date. On the placard you can:

  • Tap ⓘ for the full museum label: medium, dimensions, credit line and a link to view the work at The Met. The label opens to exactly its own height; swipe down to close it.
  • Tap Share to make a framed card for Stories or posts (see Sharing).
  • Tap Done to hang it in your gallery and return to the home screen.

Every few milestones (10, 25, 50, 100 paintings and beyond) Done opens a small celebration first.

title: What will you focus on? Setting an intention
seo: Setting a focus intention in Easel: What will you focus on?
desc: Give each Easel session a purpose: type an intention, reuse a recent one, or choose a subject like Study, Work, Writing or Reading. Your intention travels with the painting into your gallery.
card: Give each Easel session a purpose: type an intention, reuse a recent one, or choose a subject like Study, Work, Writing or Reading.
lede: Every painting in Easel is earned for something. Naming what you’re about to work on makes a session easier to start, and later your gallery remembers what each painting was for.
body:
Type it in

On the home screen, tap What will you focus on? and type a short line, like “Finish the chapter draft”. Press Go on the keyboard to begin straight away. Intentions can be up to 60 characters, and the line stays filled in for your next session, ready for the next block of the same task.

Or let Easel ask

If the line is empty when you tap Begin, Easel opens a full-screen question: What will you focus on? Under it you’ll see the session about to start (for example 25 minutes · All paintings), then two rooms:

  1. Lately: your three most recent intentions, one tap to reuse.
  2. A subject: Study, Work, Writing, Reading, Creating, Planning, Practice or Thinking.

Choosing one begins the session. To go back without starting, tap ‹ at the top left.

Where your intention appears

  • Faintly under the timer during the session.
  • On the Live Activity, on your Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.
  • In your gallery, as “For: …” on the painting’s page.
  • On the share card, if you share that painting.
Private

Your intentions are stored only on your device. Easel never sends the text anywhere. See the privacy policy.

title: Using Easel as a Pomodoro timer
seo: Pomodoro timer with paintings: how Pomodoro works in Easel
desc: Easel’s Pomodoro mode: four 25-minute focus blocks with 5-minute breaks, a new painting revealed in every block. How to start, skip a break and end a set.
card: Easel’s Pomodoro mode: four 25-minute focus blocks with 5-minute breaks, a new painting revealed in every block.
lede: Pomodoro breaks long work into focused blocks with short rests between them. In Easel, every block reveals its own painting, so a full set leaves four new works in your gallery.
body:
How a Pomodoro set works

  • Four focus blocks of 25 minutes each.
  • A 5-minute break after each of the first three blocks.
  • A new painting in every block, each revealed from fog like a single session.

Starting a set

  1. On the home screen, tap Pomodoro.
  2. Choose a collection under Focus with, if you like.
  3. Tap Begin. The focus question shows the set as 4 × 25 min.

During a break

When a block ends, its painting is revealed and saved, and your break begins. The break screen shows the painting you just earned and a countdown. Rest, stretch, look at the painting. When you’re ready, tap Begin next focus; you can start before the break is over.

Ending a set early

Tap End during a block or a break. Blocks you’ve already finished stay in your gallery; the block in progress doesn’t count.

Tip

Pomodoro completions are celebrated with their own haptic pattern when the fourth painting is revealed. Turn haptics on or off in Settings → During a session.

title: Choosing which paintings you focus with
seo: Easel collections: European paintings, Japanese prints, flowers & birds
desc: Focus with all 606 paintings or choose a collection in Easel: European Paintings, Japanese Prints, American Paintings, Flowers & Birds, a single artist like Hokusai or Rembrandt, or an era.
card: Focus with all 606 paintings or choose a collection in Easel: European Paintings, Japanese Prints, American Paintings, Flowers & Birds, a single artist like Hokusai or Rembrandt, or an era.
lede: Easel’s paintings come from a hand-picked selection of over 600 public-domain works in The Met’s collection. You can let Easel surprise you, or focus with one style, artist or era.
body:
Choose a collection

  1. On the home screen, tap the card under Focus with (it reads All paintings at first).
  2. Pick a collection. Each row shows how many of its works you’ve uncovered, like 22 / 90.
  3. Tap Done. Your next sessions draw only from that collection, until you change it.

By style

  • European Paintings: Rembrandt, Vermeer, Van Gogh, Cézanne, Corot, Courbet, Manet, Renoir, Degas and more.
  • Japanese Prints: Katsushika Hokusai, Utagawa Hiroshige and other Edo and Meiji masters.
  • American Paintings: Hudson River School landscapes by Kensett, Inness, Church and others.
  • Flowers & Birds: John James Audubon, Ogata Kōrin and botanical masters.

By artist and by era

Below the styles, the sheet lists artists with several works in Easel, and eras from the Renaissance to the Modern era (1880 onward). Choose one to spend a week with Hokusai, or a month in the nineteenth century.

How the paintings are chosen

Every work is in the public domain and comes from The Met’s Open Access collection. The selection favours celebrated works and is curated to be calm and suitable for everyone: Easel never picks a painting at random from the museum’s whole collection.

title: Your gallery of earned paintings
seo: Your Easel gallery: every painting you’ve uncovered
desc: Every painting you reveal in Easel hangs in your gallery. Open one to see it large, read its museum label, see what you focused on, and share it.
card: Every painting you reveal in Easel hangs in your gallery.
lede: Each finished session hangs its painting in your gallery. Over weeks it becomes a quiet record of everything you’ve made time for.
body:
Opening the gallery

Tap the gallery button at the top left of the home screen. The gallery slides in from the left; tap ‹ to slide it back.

Paintings are arranged newest first. At the bottom, a card shows your total time in focus, paintings and current streak; tap it to open Statistics.

A painting’s page

Tap any painting to open its page: the work large, then its museum label (title, date, artist, medium, dimensions and more from The Met), then Your visit: the day and time you uncovered it, and what it was for.

  • Tap Share (top right) to make a framed card. See Sharing.
  • Without a connection, the page shows what’s saved on your device and a short note that more details need the internet.

Sharing the whole gallery

The share button at the top right of the gallery makes a collage card of your latest paintings.

title: Sharing a painting you uncovered
seo: How to share a painting from Easel to Instagram Stories and more
desc: Share any painting you earned in Easel as a framed card, in Story (9:16) or Post (4:5) format. Save it to Photos or send it to Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, Messages and more.
card: Share any painting you earned in Easel as a framed card, in Story (9:16) or Post (4:5) format.
lede: Every painting you uncover can become a small celebration: a card with the painting in a gilded frame and how long you focused for it.
body:
Make a card

  1. Tap Share: on the finished painting at 0:00, on a painting’s page in your gallery, on the gallery itself, on a milestone or at the end of Year in Review.
  2. Choose Story (9:16) for Stories and Reels, or Post (4:5) for feeds.
  3. Tap Save to add it to Photos, or Share to open the share sheet.

Instagram, TikTok, X and others

Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, Messages, WhatsApp and Mail all appear under Share, as long as the app is installed. When the destination accepts text, Easel adds a short line and a link to the App Store with the card.

Saving to Photos

The first time you tap Save, iOS asks to let Easel add to your photo library. Easel can only add images; it can’t see or read your photos. If you declined, turn it on in the iPhone Settings app under Apps → Easel → Photos.

title: Statistics, streaks and milestones
seo: Focus statistics and streaks in Easel
desc: How Easel counts your focus time, paintings and streaks: the week chart, the 16-week focus calendar, your current and best streak, and milestones at 10, 25, 50 and 100 paintings.
card: How Easel counts your focus time, paintings and streaks: the week chart, the 16-week focus calendar, your current and best streak, and milestones at 10, 25, 50 and 100 paintings.
lede: Easel keeps a calm record of your focus: time, paintings, streaks, a week at a glance and a calendar of every day you showed up.
body:
Opening Statistics

Open the gallery and tap the card at the bottom (time · paintings · streak). Statistics rises from the bottom of the screen; tap ⌄ to close it. On iPad with a keyboard, press ⌘⇧S.

What you’ll see

  • Time in focus: the total of all completed sessions.
  • Current streak and best streak: consecutive days with at least one completed session.
  • Past seven days: a bar per day, today on the right.
  • The last 16 weeks (26 on iPad): each square is a day; deeper ink means more time in focus.
  • Paintings: how many different works you’ve uncovered, and how many sessions you’ve completed.

How streaks are counted

A day counts when you complete at least one session. Your current streak stays alive through today, so a streak from yesterday isn’t broken until the day is over. Sessions ended early don’t count.

Milestones

At 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1,000 paintings, Easel pauses for a moment: your three latest paintings, fanned in gilt frames, and the number. You can share it, or continue.

And every December there’s Year in Review.

title: Year in Review: your year in focus
seo: Easel Year in Review: your year of focus as an exhibition
desc: Every December, Easel’s Year in Review turns your year of focus into a short exhibition: hours in focus, paintings revealed, your favourite artist, longest streak and the painting of the year.
card: Every December, Easel’s Year in Review turns your year of focus into a short exhibition: hours in focus, paintings revealed, your favourite artist, longest streak and the painting of the year.
lede: Every December, Easel looks back on your year as a short, self-playing exhibition, set to Handel’s Water Music, ending with a card you can share.
body:
When it appears

From 15 December to 2 January each year, an invitation appears at the top of Statistics: “Your year in Easel”, with Enter the exhibition. In January it looks back on the year that just ended. Sessions up to 31 December are always included.

If notifications are on, Easel sends at most three gentle reminders in that season: on 15 December, 30 December and 2 January.

What’s inside

  1. The year.
  2. Your hours in focus, and when you focus best (morning, afternoon or evening).
  3. Paintings revealed, and the artist you kept most.
  4. Your longest run of days, and your fullest month.
  5. The painting of the year: the one you earned with your longest single focus.
  6. A thank-you, and a gilded card of your year to share as a Story or post.

Watching it

  • It plays by itself, a few seconds per page.
  • Tap the right side to skip ahead, the left side to go back.
  • Touch and hold to pause.
  • Swipe down to close.
  • With VoiceOver, swipe to move between pages.

title: Widgets, Live Activities, Siri and Control Center
seo: Easel widgets: Painting of the Day, Live Activity and Control Center
desc: Add Easel’s Painting of the Day and Focus & Streak widgets to your Home Screen, Lock Screen or StandBy, follow sessions in a Live Activity, and start focusing from Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center.
card: Add Easel’s Painting of the Day and Focus & Streak widgets to your Home Screen, Lock Screen or StandBy, follow sessions in a Live Activity, and start focusing from Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center.
lede: Easel lives beyond the app: a painting of the day that clears as you focus, your streak at a glance, a countdown on your Lock Screen, and a button in Control Center.
body:
Painting of the Day widget

Each morning a new painting hangs in the widget, hidden in fog. Every minute of focus clears a little more, from the centre outward. Reach your daily goal and it’s fully revealed, with its title and artist.

Set the goal in Settings → Your daily ritual → Focus each day: 15 to 120 minutes, 25 by default.

Adding a widget

  1. Touch and hold an empty area of your Home Screen until the apps jiggle.
  2. Tap Edit (or +) at the top, then Add Widget.
  3. Search for Easel, choose Painting of the Day or Focus & Streak, pick a size and tap Add Widget.

Both widgets also come in Lock Screen sizes (customise your Lock Screen and tap the widget area), and the small size works in StandBy.

Live Activity and Dynamic Island

When a session starts, Easel shows its countdown on the Lock Screen and, on iPhones that have one, in the Dynamic Island, with your intention and a softly blurred hint of the painting. When the session ends it shows the painting revealed.

Not seeing it? In the iPhone Settings app, open Apps → Easel and make sure Live Activities is on.

Siri and Shortcuts

Say “Start a focus session in Easel”, “Start focusing with Easel” or “Reveal a painting in Easel”. In the Shortcuts app, the Start Focus action can set a length from 5 to 120 minutes, handy for automations.

Control Center (iOS 18 and later)

Open Control Center, tap +, then Add a Control, and search for Easel. One tap opens Easel and begins with your current choice.

title: Daily reminders and notifications
seo: Easel daily focus reminder and notifications
desc: Turn on Easel’s gentle daily reminder, choose its time, and learn which other notifications Easel can send and how to turn each one off.
card: Turn on Easel’s gentle daily reminder, choose its time, and learn which other notifications Easel can send and how to turn each one off.
lede: Easel can send one gentle note a day to bring you back to your focus, naming that day’s painting. Notifications are always optional.
body:
Daily reminder

  1. Open Settings (top right of the home screen).
  2. In II · Your daily ritual, turn on Daily reminder. iOS asks for permission the first time.
  3. Choose a time (9:00 by default).

If you’ve already focused that day, or the time has passed, the reminder moves to tomorrow. You can also turn it on from the last page of the introduction.

Other notifications

  • Year in Review: up to three notes in its season (15 December, 30 December, 2 January), only if you focused that year.
  • Saturday note: a short weekly word, on Saturday mornings, about supporting Easel. Turn it off any time in Settings → Support → Saturday note. It stops by itself once you’ve tipped.

Easel never sends notifications unless you’ve allowed them.

Turning notifications off

Switch off the individual notes in Easel’s Settings, or turn off all of them in the iPhone Settings app under Apps → Easel → Notifications.

title: Settings: day and night, sounds, language
seo: Easel settings: dark mode, sounds, haptics and language
desc: A tour of Easel’s Settings: By day, By night or Automatic appearance, ambient music, sound effects and haptics, daily goal, language, the introduction, privacy and feedback.
card: A tour of Easel’s Settings: By day, By night or Automatic appearance, ambient music, sound effects and haptics, daily goal, language, the introduction, privacy and feedback.
lede: Easel’s Settings are laid out like an exhibition guide: today’s painting at the top, then numbered rooms of preferences.
body:
Opening Settings

Tap the gear at the top right of the home screen. Settings slides in from the right; tap ‹ to close it. On iPad with a keyboard, press ⌘,.

The rooms

  1. The gallery: Appearance. By day is a warm, lit wall; By night a deep charcoal room; Automatic follows your iPhone’s light and dark setting.
  2. During a session: ambient music, sound effects, haptic feedback.
  3. Your daily ritual: Focus each day (the goal that clears the Painting of the Day widget) and the daily reminder.
  4. Support: Become a Patron and the Saturday note.
  5. About Easel: language, about the maker, show the introduction again, privacy policy, and feedback.

Language

Easel speaks English, Polish, Spanish, French, Simplified Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Brazilian Portuguese. Tap Language in Settings to open iOS’s page for Easel and choose one; Easel restarts in the new language.

See the introduction again

Tap Show introduction in About Easel to replay the four-page tour of how Easel works.

title: Patronage: supporting Easel
seo: Is Easel free? Patronage and optional tips
desc: Easel is free, with no ads and no subscription. If you’d like to support it, you can leave a one-time tip: A Fine Brush, A Box of Pigments or A Gilded Frame. Tips unlock nothing.
card: Easel is free, with no ads and no subscription.
lede: Easel is free and made by one person. Every gallery has its patrons; if Easel brings some calm to your days, you can become one of them. Only if you’d like to.
body:
The gifts

Open Settings → Support → Become a Patron. There are three one-time gifts:

  • A Fine Brush: for the small, careful strokes that make the app better.
  • A Box of Pigments: fresh colour for whatever comes next.
  • A Gilded Frame: hangs the whole work on the wall. A true patron’s gift.

Prices are shown in your local currency by the App Store.

What a tip does

Nothing changes in the app: everything in Easel is already yours. Tips are one-time purchases, never subscriptions, and are handled entirely by Apple. Once you’ve tipped, the Saturday note stops.

Other ways to help that cost nothing: rate Easel on the App Store, share a painting, or send an idea on the feedback board.

title: Troubleshooting and finding your way
seo: Easel help: troubleshooting and finding your way around
desc: Help for Easel: getting back to the home screen, a painting that won’t load, a missing Live Activity or reminder, the widget fog not clearing, keyboard shortcuts on iPad, and how to contact us.
card: Help for Easel: getting back to the home screen, a painting that won’t load, a missing Live Activity or reminder, the widget fog not clearing, keyboard shortcuts on iPad, and how to contact us.
lede: Something not where you expected? Start here. If your question isn’t answered, write to us, and we’ll help.
body:
Getting back to the home screen

  • Gallery and Settings close with ‹ at the top left (or a swipe from the edge). The gallery slides back to the left, Settings to the right.
  • Statistics closes with ⌄ at the top left.
  • Sheets (collections, share, museum label) close with Done or a swipe down.
  • The focus question closes with ‹ without starting a session.
  • During a session, End (then confirm) returns you home.
  • On iPad with a keyboard, Esc goes back from anywhere.

“The painting couldn’t be loaded”

Easel downloads each new painting before the session starts, so it needs an internet connection when you tap Begin. Check your connection and tap Try Again. Paintings you’ve already seen are kept on your device, so your gallery still works offline.

No Live Activity on the Lock Screen

Open the iPhone Settings app → Apps → Easel and turn on Live Activities. If you tapped Don’t Allow on the first prompt, this is where to change it.

The daily reminder doesn’t arrive

  • Check that notifications are on in the iPhone Settings app → Apps → Easel → Notifications.
  • If you’ve already focused today, the reminder waits until tomorrow. That’s by design.
  • Focus modes and Scheduled Summary can hold notifications back.

The widget’s fog isn’t clearing

Only completed sessions clear the fog; sessions ended early don’t. Your daily goal is set in Settings → Focus each day. Widgets refresh when Easel saves a session; if one seems stuck, open Easel once.

My streak reset

A streak counts consecutive days with at least one completed session. A day with no completed session ends it. Your best streak is kept in Statistics.

Keyboard shortcuts on iPad

KeysDoes
ReturnBegin a session; Done when a painting is revealed
EscEnd a session (with confirmation), close a panel
⌘ GOpen the gallery
⌘ ,Open Settings
⌘ ⇧ SOpen Statistics

Moving to a new iPhone

Your gallery and history live on your device. They move with an iPhone backup or a direct transfer to a new iPhone; Easel has no account or server of its own. Deleting Easel deletes them.

Still stuck?

Write to adam@easelfocus.app, or post on the feedback board. You can also browse questions and answers.
